## Sharing qualitative data, in numbers

- **96% never deposited.** Of 425 surveyed qualitative researchers in the US, 96% have never shared qualitative data in a repository (Mozersky et al. 2021)
- **Participants are more open than researchers.** The vast majority of 30 interviewed participants of sensitive interview studies support sharing, deidentified and among researchers (Mozersky et al. 2020)
- **"Available on request" rarely holds.** In an audit of 190 articles, 74% of datasets were unavailable (Asmundo et al. 2024), and only 31% of on-request promises were honoured when tested (Archer et al. 2025)
- **Where an archive exists, reuse happens.** 7,155 downloads of 267 qualitative collections at the UK Data Service, 2002-2016; 60% of collections reused at least once, three quarters of downloads for teaching and learning (Bishop and Kuula-Luumi 2017)

::: {.notes}
The gap runs in both directions: researchers hold back although participants support sharing, and informal promises do not deliver. Infrastructure does: where a curated archive exists, the data get used, mostly in teaching. Full sources with abstracts are in the Zotero collection jurapark-workshop; the audits come from health and clinical fields because that is where such audits exist, and no transdisciplinary-specific audit was found (stating that openly is itself credible).
:::

- Bishop, L., & Kuula-Luumi, A. (2017). Revisiting qualitative data reuse: A decade on. *SAGE Open*, January-March 2017, 1-15. <https://doi.org/10.1177/2158244016685136>
